item.text:
Continued. I added a client-side failover investigation, since EPaxos is leaderless and routes proposals through `ClosestId`.

`TestAuditFindClosestSkipsDeadReplica` uses a fake `ping` executable and replicas `10.0.0.1..3` with the co-located replica dead:

```
replicas=[10.0.0.1 10.0.0.2 10.0.0.3] alive=[false true true] ClosestId=0 Ping=[1 1]
ClosestId=0 selects a dead or invalid replica; want one of the alive ids 1 or 2
```

The fallback iterates over `c.Ping` and assigns the Ping-slice index to `ClosestId`; after a dead replica is skipped, that index is not the replica id. `SendProposal` then indexes `c.writers[0]`, which is nil because the client only connects to alive replicas, so the client can panic on this failover path.

Also newly strengthened:

- F18 now includes a real `Propose` round trip: the truncated 70 KB value leaves its bytes in the stream and the following timestamp is decoded as `6510615555426900570` instead of `123456789`.
- The critical F1 reproduction remains the all-alive state-machine divergence: replica 0 retains the chosen PUT while replicas 1-4 execute NOOP.

Current status: four cluster controls pass; 30 epaxos finding tests fail; the separate client failover test also fails; `go build ./...` passes; implementation files remain byte-identical to `../source`.
